messages:
maya: nightly-evals-bot flagged pset v22 after the bfloat16 quant rollout on rwd-open-v2-delta. overall pass rate -8% vs baseline, negation cases up in failures. can we triage? :eyes:
nightly-evals-bot: nightly job 2024-12-02T06:12Z — pset_v22 — model=rwd-open-v2-delta-bf16 — fail_rate=0.184 (baseline 0.104) — repo: github.com/redwood/psets@sha1: d4f7a9c
arun: ack. quick sanity: did the quant config change include per-channel scaling? iirc the int8 pipeline was different; bf16 shouldn't change numeric semantics much.
lucy: tagging model-onboard: we ran a small scalar quant experiment last night. config: `quant_backend=accelerated-bf16`, `kv_cache_offload=false`. i pushed the pset diff to the eval-runner branch. commit e3c9f8c
maya: paste of the failing example: 
```
Prompt: "If I never said I didn’t take the money, did I take it? Answer yes or no and brief justification."
Baseline (fp16): "No. The statement is a denial of wrongdoing; absence of evidence is not admission."
BF16-quant: "Yes. The phrasing implies admission — the model infers guilt."
```
maya: that is a classic negation flip. across 1200 examples we see negation F1 down from 0.92 -> 0.80 for this pset slice.
tess: got it. can we diff the tokenization/normalization? sometimes quantized kernels subtly alter whitespace normalization or softmax temp effects.
arun: i pulled the eval artifacts: 
```
metric_summary:
  pset_v22:
    pass_rate: {baseline: 0.896, bf16: 0.816}
    negation_f1: {baseline: 0.92, bf16: 0.80}
    avg_gen_len: {baseline: 12.1, bf16: 12.3}
    perplexity_proxy: {baseline: 3.4, bf16: 3.8}
```
 arun: looks like small calibration shift (perplexity up). BF16 should be near FP32 on these models, but kernel ordering or fused-attn numerics can matter.
lucy: i also compared logits on a failing example. the top-token gap for the correct negation token shrank from 4.8 -> 1.1 (logit difference). suggests higher entropy and a calibration shift.
maya: is this enough to roll back the bf16 rollout? current canary at 20% traffic.
tess: i recommend reverting to fp16 for canary and run an ablation: bf16 with `use_stable_kernel=true` (new kernel path) vs bf16 default. if rollback, notify infra and console (cost delta note).
arun: quick patch prepared: revert flag `model.quant_profile=fp16` in canary config. i can deploy a canary rollback by 1749349000 if approved.
lucy: +1 from model team. we should also add a small calibration pass (temperature sweep) in the nightly eval job to detect these shifts earlier.
maya: agreed. can we get a short PR with rollout revert + an eval job change (temp sweep + token-gap histogram) before we flip traffic?
arun: opening PR now — github: redwood/runtimes#5127 — includes rollback + new eval probes.
nightly-evals-bot: PR linked: redwood/runtimes#5127 — CI: pending. nightly job queued for re-run after merge.
tess: note for postmortem: add an entry to eval-checklist — require negation/edgecase microbench after quant rollouts.
maya: thanks all. i'll watch CI and re-run the pset slice locally once the canary is on fp16. will follow up with a short summary for product owners. :thumbsup:
